title: Electromagnetic Induction
source_note: NCERT Class 12 Physics Part I, Reprint 2026-27 (RATIONALISED 2022-23) -- current CBSE syllabus. Equations NOT reliable in this extraction; use board frames as the equation source of truth.

sections.heading: The Experiments Of Faraday And Henry

summary:
1. ΦB = B.A = BA cos θ
2. ε = –N dΦB/dt (Faraday's law)
3. Lenz's law: induced emf opposes flux change (energy conservation)
4. Motional emf: ε = Blv
5. Inductance = flux-linkage/current = NΦ/I
6. Mutual inductance: ε1 = –M12 dI2/dt, M12 = M21
7. Self-inductance: ε = –L dI/dt
8. Long solenoid: L = μr μ0 n² A l
9. AC generator: ε = NBA(2πν) sin(2πνt)
points_to_ponder:
1. Oersted/Ampere (moving charge→field) then Faraday/Henry ~1830 (moving magnet→current) — deep symmetry.
2. Induced currents oppose flux change per energy conservation (closed circuit); open circuit induces emf across ends.
3. Motional emf explainable via Lorentz force (moving charge) OR via time-varying B inducing E even for stationary charge — hints at relativity principle relevance to Faraday's law.
exercises:
(6.1-6.8): direction of induced current (Lenz's law) in various geometries; solenoid+loop emf calc; rectangular loop emf on exit from field; rotating rod emf; falling horizontal wire emf; self-inductance from current-change/emf data; mutual inductance flux-linkage change.

Named scientists: Michael Faraday, Joseph Henry (1797-1878, Princeton, Smithsonian first director, electromagnet improvements, electromagnetic motor, self-induction discovery), Heinrich Friedrich Lenz, Nicola Tesla.
